title: Booking a Third-Party Recovery on a Travel Protection Policy
content:
Where a liable third party has paid the traveller for a loss a policy of the Travel Protection Plans has
already settled, the insurer recovers what it paid, and the recovery restores the benefit that settlement
consumed. The recovery is booked by the agency against the payment it partly reverses; the decision already made
on the claim is untouched, and nothing is returned to or taken from the traveller.

## What the policyholder sees afterwards

That much of the benefit stands available again on the policy for the rest of its term.

## How the write is made

The desk unlocks the agency-side tool `book_benefit_recovery_c1be7196` and calls it. One call adds a recovery
row to the policy's claim record: it carries the recovered money as a negative movement of the benefit account,
marks the claim recovered, stamps the date it was received and points at the payment it partly reverses.

## The parameters

| Parameter | What it is |
|---|---|
| `care_policy_id` | The reference number of the travel protection policy whose benefit is restored, read from the policy record found for the traveller |
| `source_claim_id` | The reference number of the payment row this recovery partly reverses, read from the claim record of that policy |
| `claim_reference` | The reference the insurer quoted for the claim the money was recovered on, copied character for character from the claim record, keeping the original wording, digits and punctuation, with no translation, normalisation, summarisation, addition or deletion |
| `claim_type` | The benefit the restored money was paid under; exactly one of the eleven heads below and never any other word |
| `recovered_amount_usd` | The money recovered from the third party for that settled loss, given as a positive USD amount with 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent; the row itself carries it as a negative movement of the benefit account |

The eleven heads `claim_type` accepts are `trip_cancellation`, where the journey was called off before it began;
`trip_interruption`, where a journey already begun was cut short or broken into; `medical_emergency`, where the
traveller was treated for illness or injury away from home; `dental_emergency`, where the treatment was dental;
`evacuation`, where the traveller had to be moved or repatriated for medical reasons; `baggage_delay`, where
checked baggage reached the traveller late; `baggage_loss`, where baggage or an article in it was lost or
damaged outright; `travel_delay`, where the traveller themselves was held up in transit; `missed_connection`,
where a late arrival caused an onward service to be missed; `rental_damage`, where a hired vehicle was damaged;
and `cancel_for_any_reason`, where the journey was called off for a reason no other head covers.

## What comes back

A plain-text confirmation naming the reference number minted for the recovery row, the policy it was booked
against and the recovered amount as it now stands on the claim record. Receiving that confirmation is what
indicates the recovery has been booked and the benefit restored; nothing else is returned.
